title: Colour the Map With k Colours

concept.title: Colour the vertices one by one, checking only the earlier neighbours
body: Colour the `n` vertices of a graph with `k` colours so that **two vertices joined by an edge never get the same colour**. The search colours the vertices in the order 0, 1, 2, ... For vertex `v`, a colour is allowed if none of the neighbours **that are already coloured** (the ones with a smaller number) has it. Neighbours with a larger number will check against `v` later.

The colours are **labelled** (colour 1 and colour 2 are different), so swapping two colours in a colouring gives another colouring. Note that `color[v]` is simply overwritten by the next try and needs no undo, because the later vertices only look at vertices with smaller numbers, which are always up to date. Without edges the answer is `k^n`, which is the largest case.

statement: A graph has `n` vertices numbered 1 to `n` and `m` edges. Count the ways to colour every vertex with one of `k` colours so that the two ends of every edge have different colours. The colours are different from each other (swapping two colours gives a different colouring).
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two vertices joined by an edge.
constraints: 0 <= m <= n * (n - 1) / 2, no repeated edges and no loops

examples.note: A triangle needs three different colours: 3 * 2 * 1 = 6 colourings.

hints: Colour the vertices in order 1, 2, ..., n.
A colour is allowed if no earlier neighbour has it.
You do not need to undo the colour of a vertex: the next try overwrites it.

starter.python:
n, m, k = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: Vertices are coloured in order; a colour is tried only when no earlier neighbour has it. Reaching vertex `n` completes a colouring. Overwriting `color[v]` replaces an undo step.
solution.complexity: Time O(k^n) in the worst case (no edges), space O(n).
